notes: Translated from OVAL access_control/duty1-3. OVAL's state of the world is an event log; the compensate row becomes one evidence record with its payAmount as an evidence parameter, and the play row is the request. OVAL's request names no party; the log's actor, ex:William_Hall, is made the assignee, so the duty's bearer is defined (the duty and its Offer-level permission name no assignee, so the bearer is the request subject, workflows §5.3). Dropped: OVAL's separate untargeted permission for compensate, which exists only to make the payment event itself compliant in monitoring mode and is not ODRL 2.2 (IM 2.6.1 requires a target). odrl:unit was a string literal; IM 2.5.1 makes it an IRI. This is the first corpus case with a witness-source operand, and it uses the duty-action refinement form that due2-profiles.md §9 #6 asks about: with an explicit binding of odrl:payAmount to due2:witnessSource the refinement is an ordinary witness condition and needs no new machinery; #6 reduces to whether due2-core should ship that binding as a baseline. OVAL parameterises duties: under its default (semantics_for_duties=1) a permission with an unfulfilled duty is granted on the promise of performance (duty2: True); under -1 it is refused (duty3: False). due2 has one reading — Pending, naming the duty — which agrees with neither as a yes/no but is what both are approximating. duty2 and duty3 have identical inputs, so they are one scenario here.
